message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"3.40","text":"Similarly, Simon seemed to show from many things in the Scriptures that God is subject to every passion. In response Peter said, “Tell me whether an evil and utterly wicked person has no desire at all to expose himself regarding the things in which he sins.” Simon said, “He has no desire to.” Peter said, “How, then, can God be evil and wicked, if it was by his own will that the evils publicly written against him were added?” Simon replied, “It is possible that, contrary to his intention, the exposure against him was written by another power.” Peter said, “First, then, let us investigate this. If he exposed himself by his own counsel, as you just agreed, he is not wicked. But if it was done by another power, the matter must be investigated—and with all our strength. It must be examined whether someone implicated him, though he is nothing but good, in all the evil things.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὁμῶς","chosen":"Similarly","rationale":"ὁμῶς can mean “likewise” or “in the same way,” linking this summary to Simon’s preceding examples."},{"source_quote":"Εἰ μηδὲν ἀγαπᾷ ὁ κακὸς καὶ πάνυ μοχθηρὸς ἐφ’ οἷς ἁμαρτάνει ἑαυτὸν ἐλέγχειν, ἀπόκριναί μοι.","chosen":"Tell me whether an evil and utterly wicked person has no desire at all to expose himself regarding the things in which he sins.","rationale":"Here εἰ introduces the proposition Peter asks Simon to confirm or deny, as Simon’s reply Οὐκ ἀγαπᾷ indicates. Although εἰ can formally introduce a condition, the exchange supports an indirect question. ἀγαπᾷ with the infinitive concerns desire or willingness, while ἐλέγχειν means exposing or convicting one’s own wrongdoing."},{"source_quote":"αὐτοῦ λείμματι","chosen":"by his own will","rationale":"The immediate contrast with παρὰ προαίρεσιν αὐτοῦ and ὑπὸ τῆς ἑαυτοῦ βουλῆς supports interpreting the printed λείμματι as an orthographic form of λήματι from λῆμα, “will” or “resolve.” The ordinary sense of λείμμα, “remainder, deficiency, or omission,” does not readily sustain Peter’s argument."},{"source_quote":"τὸν κατ’ αὐτοῦ γραφῆναι ἔλεγχον","chosen":"the exposure against him was written","rationale":"ἔλεγχος can mean refutation, censure, conviction, or exposure; “exposure” preserves the connection with the written disclosure of traits alleged to be blameworthy."},{"source_quote":"αὐτὸν μόνον ἀγαθὸν ὄντα","chosen":"though he is nothing but good","rationale":"The main rendering takes μόνον adverbially with ἀγαθόν, emphasizing the absence of evil in God; this is favored by the immediate contrast with the evil things attributed to him. Because μόνον formally agrees with αὐτόν, an alternative is “though he alone is good,” excluding goodness from others."},{"source_quote":"ἐξεταστέον μή τις αὐτὸν μόνον ἀγαθὸν ὄντα ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς κακοῖς ὑπέβαλεν.","chosen":"It must be examined whether someone implicated him, though he is nothing but good, in all the evil things.","rationale":"μή introduces the matter to be examined. ὑποβάλλειν with ἐπί can describe putting someone under adverse things or charges and thus bringing that person under suspicion or implicating that person. Because the surrounding argument concerns evil statements publicly written against God and asks who authored them, “implicated him … in” is chosen as a false-attribution sense rather than as a claim that God was made to undergo actual evils. A more literal alternative is “whether someone subjected him, though he is nothing but good, to all the evil things,” which may suggest actual exposure to evils; in this context it can also be understood as subjection to allegations of those evils."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"λείμματι","issue":"The confirmed printed form ordinarily points to λείμμα, “remainder, deficiency, or omission,” but the immediate contrasts with “contrary to his intention” and “by his own counsel” strongly suggest an orthographic form of λήματι from λῆμα, “will” or “resolve.” This remains a contextual proposal rather than an alteration of the selected edition’s Greek.","proposed_reading":"λήματι","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
